n1.point: Complainant HydraFacial LLC (formerly Edge Systems LLC) is a California limited liability company headquartered at 2165 E. Spring Street, Long Beach, CA 90806, engaged in the design, development, manufacture, and sale of hydrodermabrasion systems.
n1.quote: Complainant HydraFacial LLC f/k/a Edge Systems LLC is a California limited liability company having its principal place of business at 2165 E. Spring Street, Long Beach, CA 90806.

n10.point: Hydrodermabrasion systems for skin treatment deliver liquid solutions (containing alpha hydroxy acid, beta hydroxy acid, antioxidants, and moisturizers) to skin using a handpiece tip contacting the patient's skin, with vacuum source drawing solution from a container through the handpiece to the skin and then away for disposal.
n10.quote: These hydrodermabrasion systems are configured to deliver various liquid solutions—such as those containing alpha hydroxy acid, beta hydroxy acid, antioxidants, and moisturizers—to the skin of a patient using a handpiece with a tip that contacts the patient's skin

n11.point: HydraFacial manufactures the HydraFacial Syndeo system, HydraFacial Elite system, and HydraFacial Allegro system as patented hydrodermabrasion systems, along with tips, accessories, liquid solutions, and boosters for skin treatments.
n11.quote: HydraFacial designs, develops, manufactures , and sells other patented hydrodermabrasion systems, including the HydraFacial Elite system and the HydraFacial Allegro system.

n12.point: U.S. Patent No. 11,446,477 (the '477 Patent) issued on September 20, 2022, from Application No. 16/517,268 filed July 19, 2019, claiming priority to provisional applications filed December 30, 2005 and February 2, 2006, with expiration date March 29, 2026. HydraFacial owns the entire right, title, and interest by assignment.
n12.quote: HydraFacial owns by assignment the entire right, title, and interest in the ' 477 Patent, which duly and lawfully issued on September 20, 2022. The '477 Patent issued from U.S. Patent Application No. 16/517,268, filed July 19, 2019.

n13.point: U.S. Patent No. 12,053,607 (the '607 Patent) issued on August 6, 2024, from Application No. 18/487,916 filed October 16, 2023, claiming priority to provisional applications filed December 30, 2005 and February 2, 2006, with expiration date March 29, 2026. HydraFacial owns the entire right, title, and interest by assignment.

n14.point: Asserted claims of the '607 Patent are claims 1, 2-10, 11, 12-13, 15-19, 20 (with claims 1, 11, and 15 being independent claims).

n15.point: The complaint alleges respondents directly infringe the '477 and '607 Patents, either literally or under the doctrine of equivalents, through the Bela MD, Cleopatra, and MIRApeel systems.
n15.quote: Respondents directly infringe, literally or under the doctrine of equivalents, and/or induce or contribute to the infringement of, at least the following claims (collectively, "the Asserted Claims") of the Asserted Patents via the Accused Products

n16.point: The complaint alleges respondents induce infringement by recommending, encouraging, instructing, and suggesting customers use the accused products in an infringing manner, and that respondents have knowledge of the asserted patents from cease-and-desist letters sent prior to filing.
n16.quote: Respondents also induce the infringement of the Asserted Patents by recommending, encouraging, instructing, and/or suggesting that its customers use the Accused Products in an infringing manner. n17.point: The complaint alleges respondents offer for sale and/or sell within the United States, and/or import into the United States, the accused products which constitute material parts of the invention that are not staple articles of commerce suitable for substantial non-infringing use and are known by respondents to be especially made or adapted for use in infringement.

n53.point: To prove prosecution laches, the accused infringer must show: (1) unreasonable and inexcusable delay under the totality of circumstances, and (2) prejudice to the accused infringer from the delay, citing Cancer Research Technology Ltd. v. Barr Laboratories, 625 F.3d 724.

about.text: Complainant HydraFacial LLC (formerly Edge Systems LLC), of Long Beach, California, designs, develops, manufactures, and sells hydrodermabrasion systems, including the HydraFacial Syndeo, Elite, and Allegro systems, along with tips, accessories, liquid solutions, and boosters. Hydrodermabrasion systems treat skin by delivering liquid solutions (containing alpha and beta hydroxy acids, antioxidants, and moisturizers) through a handpiece tip that contacts the patient's skin, using a vacuum to draw the solution from a container, across the skin, and then away for disposal. The Commission instituted this investigation based on a complaint alleging violation of Section 337 (a law barring unfair imports, including patent-infringing goods) through the importation and sale of accused hydrodermabrasion systems and subassemblies.

The respondents named in the notice of institution were Luvo Medical Technologies Inc. and Clarion Medical Technologies, Inc. (both Ontario, Canada distributors), Healthcare Markets, Inc. d/b/a Powered by MRP (Utah) and Medical Purchasing Resource, LLC (Texas), Bio-Infusions USA Inc. (Florida), MIRAmedtech UG (Germany) and MIRAmedtech SP. Z.O.O. (Poland), which manufacture and distribute the accused products, and eMIRAmed USA, LLC (California), which develops and distributes them. The investigation as instituted covered claims 1-5 and 7-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,446,477 ('the '477 patent'), titled for devices and methods for treating skin, which issued September 20, 2022 and is owned by HydraFacial. The complaint also originally asserted U.S. Patent No. 12,053,607 ('the '607 patent'), covering related claims, but that patent was later withdrawn from the investigation.

allegations.text: HydraFacial alleges that the accused Bela MD, Cleopatra, and MIRApeel hydrodermabrasion systems directly infringe the '477 and '607 patents, either literally or under the doctrine of equivalents. It further alleges that respondents induce infringement by recommending, encouraging, and instructing customers to use the accused products in an infringing manner, with knowledge of the patents from cease-and-desist letters sent before the complaint was filed, and that respondents supply components that are material parts of the invention, not staple articles of commerce, known to be especially made or adapted for infringing use.

On importation, HydraFacial alleges the Cleopatra system is assembled and manufactured in Germany and/or Poland by the MIRAmedtech entities and then imported into the United States and sold by Bio-Infusions and Medical Purchasing Resource, while the MIRApeel system is likewise made in Germany and/or Poland and imported and sold by eMIRAmed, MIRAmedtech Germany, and Medical Purchasing Resource.

For domestic industry (the complainant's U.S.-based investment or activity tied to the patented technology that Section 337 requires), HydraFacial alleges it performs all research, development, and manufacturing in the United States, holds a headquarters and a roughly 105,000-square-foot manufacturing and distribution facility in Long Beach, California, employs substantial personnel devoted to research, development, manufacturing, testing, engineering, and customer service, and has invested approximately $8.2 million, $8.4 million, and $10.1 million in U.S. research and development in 2021, 2022, and 2023 respectively. It alleges its HydraFacial Syndeo, Elite, and Allegro systems practice at least one claim of each asserted patent.

HydraFacial seeks a permanent limited exclusion order (an order barring the named respondents' infringing products from U.S. entry) under Section 337(d) covering the Bela MD, Cleopatra, and MIRApeel systems and their components, and asks that the Commission require a bond during the 60-day Presidential review period under Section 337(j) for any such imports.

paragraphs.text: Luvo Medical Technologies, joined by Clarion Medical Technologies and Healthcare Markets d/b/a Powered by MRP, denied violating Section 337 and denied that the '477 patent's asserted claims are valid and enforceable. Luvo admitted selling the Bela MD for importation but denied importing it or selling it after importation, and denied selling or importing the Cleopatra or MIRApeel systems, arguing the Bela MD does not meet claim limitations such as the 'manifold system' and 'supply conduit' requirements and that indirect infringement was not shown absent direct infringement. Luvo asserted invalidity under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102, 103, and 112 based on prior art references including the Karasiuk, Shadduck, Burdorff, and Coleman patents and other publications, and also raised a prosecution laches defense, contending HydraFacial used a serial filing strategy with placeholder claims over roughly seventeen years between the patent family's priority filings and the '477 patent's issuance, prejudicing Luvo and other market participants. Luvo also argued HydraFacial failed to adequately allege a domestic industry and failed to state a claim, and asked the Commission to deny all relief.

answers.who: Luvo Medical Technologies, Inc.; Clarion Medical Technologies, Inc.; Healthcare Markets, Inc. d/b/a Powered by MRP

decisions.text: Before the case reached a full hearing on the merits as to all respondents, the ALJ issued initial determinations finding several respondents in default for failing to respond: Medical Purchasing Resource, LLC in December 2024, and Bio-Infusions USA Inc., MIRAmedtech UG, eMIRAmed USA, LLC, and MIRAmedtech SP. Z.O.O. in January 2025.

Separately, the ALJ granted a joint motion terminating the investigation as to Clarion Medical Technologies, Inc., Healthcare Markets, Inc. d/b/a Powered by MRP, and Luvo Medical Technologies Inc. based on a settlement.

The Commission then found that claims 1-5 and 7-20 of the '477 patent were infringed by the products of the defaulting respondents (Medical Purchasing Resource, LLC, eMIRAmed USA, LLC, Bio-Infusions USA Inc., MIRAmedtech SP. Z.O.O., and MIRAmedtech UG), and found a violation of Section 337 as to those respondents.

As a remedy, the Commission issued a limited exclusion order barring entry of infringing hydrodermabrasion systems and components, and issued cease and desist orders (orders barring further U.S. sale or distribution of infringing inventory) against MIRAmedtech UG, MIRAmedtech SP. Z.O.O., Bio-Infusions USA, Inc., eMIRAmed USA, LLC, and Medical Purchasing Resource, LLC.

summary.headline: HydraFacial LLC accused several distributors and manufacturers of hydrodermabrasion skin-treatment systems of importing and selling products (Bela MD, Cleopatra, and MIRApeel systems) that infringe its patents on skin-treatment devices, and the Commission found a violation of Section 337 and issued a limited exclusion order and cease and desist orders against the defaulting respondents after the remaining answering respondents settled.

standing.text: The investigation has been terminated. Clarion Medical Technologies, Inc., Healthcare Markets, Inc. d/b/a Powered by MRP, and Luvo Medical Technologies Inc. left the case through a settlement. Medical Purchasing Resource, LLC, Bio-Infusions USA Inc., MIRAmedtech UG, eMIRAmed USA, LLC, and MIRAmedtech SP. Z.O.O. were found in default, and the Commission found them to have violated Section 337 by infringing claims 1-5 and 7-20 of the '477 patent. The remedy in force is a limited exclusion order against infringing hydrodermabrasion systems and components, together with cease and desist orders against each of the five defaulting respondents.

title: Certain Hydrodermabrasion Systems and Components Thereof III
